title: 13,000 Signed Up to Fix India’s Websites With AI (3 Real Ideas)
description:
Imagine dealing with a confusing visa application, an urgent blood-bank search, or a cybercrime complaint. Can AI-assisted building make these citizen experiences less frustrating? Around 13,000 PEOPLE REGISTERED for Build What Moves India, an independent hackathon presented by Varun Mayya in partnership with OpenAI. The organizers selected 250 builds for mentoring and 10 finalists. It does NOT mean 13,000 completed apps, and the finalist prototypes are NOT approved government services.

This original video examines three reported prototypes:
1. RaktKhoj — exploring discovery of blood banks and potential donors. Do not use an unverified prototype as an emergency service; confirm availability and eligibility with professionals.
2. Samarthan — exploring AI-assisted cybercrime complaint DRAFT preparation. Use the government portal at https://www.cybercrime.gov.in/ for actual cybercrime reports and call 1930 promptly for financial cyberfraud; don't expose OTPs or passwords.
3. Atithi — exploring simpler e-visa form guidance. Check official visa rules and fees independently.

Then learn the hackathon's grounded product-building framework: one real user problem; one complete journey; meaningful use of OpenAI Codex or its models; safe mock data where production access is unavailable; usability tests and independent factual/security checks. No government adoption is promised.

NOTE: All interface screens and process diagrams are original fictional educational illustrations, NOT actual app recordings. We did not independently run or audit the prototypes or record human voiceovers. Audio uses a synthetic natural-style voice.
